ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Particles A and B undergo uniformly accelerated linear motion on a straight line. The v-t graph is shown in the figure. At the end of 3 s, the two particles meet on the way, so what are the relative position and distance between the starting points of the two particles?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: A is 4 m ahead of B
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the graph: The figure is a v-t graph, with the vertical axis as v/(m·s^-1) and the horizontal axis as t/s. B's velocity graph line is a straight line from (0 s, 0 m/s) to (3 s, 4 m/s); A's velocity graph line is a straight line from (1 s, 0 m/s) to (3 s, 2 m/s). The figure also uses dashed lines to mark t=3 s, v=4 m/s, and v=2 m/s. Then reason: The area enclosed by the v-t graph and the time axis represents displacement. B's displacement within 0~3 s is the area of a triangle: s_B=1/2×3×4=6 m. A moves from t=1 s to t=3 s, and the displacement is the area of a triangle: s_A=1/2×(3-1)×2=2 m. The problem says that at the end of 3 s the two particles meet on the way, that is, at the end of 3 s the positions of the two are the same. B moves 6-2=4 m more than A during this period, so in order to meet in the end, A's starting point must be 4 m ahead of B's starting point along the direction of motion.
